Material Technologies.

SLA

Stereolithography, or resin 3D printing, refers to a process in which a light source cures liquid resin, hardening it layer by layer. SLA 3D printers produce parts with smoother surface finishes, tighter tolerances, and higher dimensional accuracy than other 3D printing technologies.

SLS

Selective laser sintering (SLS) is the most common additive manufacturing technology for industrial applications, trusted by engineers and manufacturers across different industries for its ability to produce strong, functional parts.

Common Questions

Form Now is Formlabs’ on-demand 3D printing service. Upload a model, get an instant quote across 28+ industrial-grade materials, and we print and ship professional parts — often in as little as 2 days.

Drag and drop your file to get an instant quote, choose a material and finish, then check out. We handle printing, post-processing, and shipping for you.

Most orders ship in 1–2 business days. Order by 2 PM ET and eligible parts ship the next business day; choose local pickup at checkout to get them even faster.

We ship across the United States, with international shipping rolling out. Available options and delivery estimates are shown at checkout.

We accept STL, STEP, OBJ, 3MF, IGES and .FORM files — just drag and drop. Your models stay secure and confidential, and you retain all rights to them.

Over 28 industrial SLA and SLS materials — from Grey, Black, and Clear resins to Tough, Flexible, and Nylon powders. Each lists key specs so you can match the right material to your part.

Maximum size depends on the technology and material. The configurator flags anything outside the build volume and suggests how to split larger models.

Engineers, designers, and makers who need professional parts fast — from one-off prototypes to small production runs — without owning a printer.
